newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
PRIME MINISTER URGES INSURGENTS TO ACCEPT TALKS OFFER

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral urged insurgent groups in the northeastern part of the country to accept the government's offer for unconditional talks. He, however, ruled out acceptance of their demand for independence. In meetings with various political parties, he said he was prepared for talks with the insurgents anywhere and indicated the government was against setting any time frame for the militants to accept the offer for talks.
Indian Express
BOFORS HOUSE COMMITTEE MEMBERS UNDER SCRUTINY

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) sought the sanction of the speaker of the lower house to interrogate members of the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) that looked into the Bofors case and cleared the former government. The CBI, however, did not specify why it wanted to question the chairman and members of the Bofors JPC. Sources said the CBI had also asked for a detailed account of witnesses who deposed before the JPC, documents furnished by the government and the way the JPC let top Bofors executives off the hook when they deposed before the committee.
The Hindustan Times
GOVERNMENT NOT KEEN TO ACT ON ANIMAL HUSBANDRY SCAM

New Delhi was likely to throw the ball back in the Bihar governor's court in the animal husbandry case, as it wanted to distance itself from the controversy. The government may dispose of the Central Bureau of lnvestigation's (CBI) request without even sending it to the president. The CBI had sought the Bihar governor's permission to chargesheet the state chief minister and others in the animal husbandry case. It also asked the president's permission to indict a union minister and some officials currentiy posted in Delhi.
The Pioneer
FISSURES WIDEN OVER WOMEN'S RESERVATION BILL

Fissures within the Janata Dal, the main constituent of the ruling coalition, over the bill seeking reservation for women in parliament and assemblies widened. The party's working president demanded that no whip be issued to members on the issue and to let them vote according to their conscience. He also reiterated his demand for proportionate representation within the scope of 33 percent reserved seats.
The Economic Times
TATAS PLAN FRESH AVIATION FORAY

Tata Industries has renewed its interest in the domestic aviation sector. The corporate started work on a fresh application for a passenger airline venture and was in touch with the Civil Aviation Ministry for information. According to sources in the ministry, the Tatas asked for details on information pertaining to the additional capacity that was available for distribution. The main reason for such information, sources said, was to make sure that its fresh application failed within the guidelines of the recently approved civil aviation policy.
ITC NET UP 31 PERCENT TO 3.42 BLN RUPEES

ITC Limited registered a 31 percent increase in net profit for the year ended March 31 at 3.43 billion rupees. The board of the company approved a capital expenditure-cum-investment plan of 19 billion rupees over the next five years. There was no mention of dividend in the company's official release. There was confusion too about the reserves position of the company, excluding revaluation reserves, which showed a blank in the official ITC statement as against 6481.1 million rupees for the year ended March 1996. ITC sources said the dividend would only be announced when the final audited results were given.
GOVERNMENT STANDS TO LOSE ON DISCLOSURE SCHEME

The revised and now enacted Voluntary Disclosure Scheme (VDS) 1997 could see the government standing to lose a sizeable revenue. The intention was to tax voluntarily disclosed income represented by assets acquired before April 1, 1987 based on the market rate prevailing on the cut-off date. The problem, it appeared, was that if voluntarily disclosed income is represented by jewellery or bullion, the disclosed income would have to be equal to the market value of such assets as on the cut off date. It seemed that a tax of 30 percent would be payable by a declarant on such market value.
Financial Express
PLAN TO REVOKE BANK GUARANTEES OF ERRING CELL OPERATORS

The Department of Telecommunication (DoT) was contemplating invoking bank guarantees of 12 cellular phone operators for their failure to pay licence fee for the second year. A status note on the progress of cellular services estimated DoT had to collect over three billion rupees from these operators. The companies had initially showed promptness in paying up the fees on time. The note said the first year's licence fees were paid by all the licensees before signing of the licence agreement.
DELHI BOURSE TO DELIST FIRMS FOR DEFAULT

In an unprecedented move, the Delhi bourse (DSE) decided to delist over 1,900 companies for violation of the listing agreement. These companies, accounting for almost 50 percent of the companies listed on the bourse, failed to pay the listing fee. The total arrears run up to 35 million rupees. If the companies failed to respond within three weeks, it would be followed up by winding up petitions in court as well as suspension of trading.
Business Standard
COGENTRIX CITES HIGHER COSTS, SEEKS FRESH CLEARANCE

U.S.-based Cogentrix Inc is seeking a fresh techno-economic clearance (TEC) for its proposed 1,000 megawatt (mw) power project in Mangalore. Cogentrix cited increased project costs due to inflation for its request for a fresh TEC. According to Cogentrix, the rupee cost of the project had escalated by 730 million rupees, while the foreign exchange component cost had risen by $20 million since the day the project received clearance. The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) had refused to grant fresh clearance to the project, arguing that as per the government notification, inflation cannot be considered a factor for cost revision.
CITIBANK SCORES A FIRST

Citibank India kicked off trading in securitised instruments by concluding the first-ever placement of auto-receivables which would be listed and traded on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) wholesale debt market. It had placed 200 million rupees worth auto loans with mutual funds on a non-recourse basis. The securitised paper with a tenure of 27 months carried a coupon rate of 15.5 percent. This was the first securitised debt issue to be listed on the NSE. In a bid to attract investors to this new instrument, Citibank also appointed Birla Marlin Securities as the market makers for the instrument.
FIVE COMPANIES TO SIGN LICENCE, INTERCONNECT PACTS

Five basic telecom companies holding letters of intent were expected to sign the licence and interconnect agreements before the end of June. This followed a joint letter of consent signed between the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and three operators who had challenged a DoT move to encash their bank guarantees. Under the terms of the letter which was expected to give the final leg-up to the three-year-old basic telecom deregulation process in the country, the companies and DoT would jointly work towards a settlement of all contentious issues.
The Observer
EXPORT GROWTH TARGET FIXED AT 20 PERCENT

The government has set an export growth target of 20 percent to achieve $40 billion in 1997/98 with the eventual aim of achieving $100 billion. Exports grew by 4.1 percent in 1996/97. In order to promote exports of the small-scale sector, a core group would be set up. The guidelines for recognition of the status of export houses/trading houses was relaxed. The norms for recognition of export house status was reduced from 200 million to 125 million rupees.
MINIMUM INITIAL LEVEL MAY BE SET AT $100 MLN

Following large-scale default on commitments by foreign companies in the automobile sector, the government decided to recast the foreign investment policy for the sector. The proposed policy, among other things, stipulates a minimum initial investment of $100 million in foreign direct investment (FDI) ventures in the sector. It also stipulates a minimum indigenisation level of 50 percent in the first two years of operations of FDI projects in the auto sector. It also proposes that the foreign investment ventures should have two-thirds of their production indigenised within a stipulated time-frame.
GOVERNMENT INTRODUCES ONE DAY TREASURY BILLS

The government has decided to introduce the auction of 14-day Treasury bills in a bid to offer investors in government debt instruments a wider range of maturities. The bills would form part of the borrowings of the government of India and they would be treated as approved investment for the purposes of statutory liquidity ratio. Commenting on the government decision, capital market analysts said that the auction of 14-day bills could be construed as an instrument for the government to intervene in the call money market.
UNIFORM LEGISLATION LIKELY FOR FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

As a step towards uniform banking legislation, the Reserve Bank of India is considering a proposal to put the three major financial institutions (FIs) -- Industrial Development Bank (IDBI), Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) and Industrial Finance Corporation (IFCI) -- under one law. The move was aimed at evolving a uniform procedure for the governance of these financial institutions. Once the leading FIs were brought under a uniform legislation, it would be easier for the central bank to frame a uniform banking legislation, more so with the RBI's present move to graduate FIs to universal banking.
